Investigation complete; event-driven gate is blocked by GitHub's trust model, not by design. Verified empirically (branch probe PR #46, main probe PR #47/#48) and against current docs/changelogs/community threads (through 2026-07-31): (1) Copilot's review fires no pull_request_review our workflows can run on; (2) its internal workflow DOES emit workflow_run — three probe runs arrived with actor 'Copilot' — but GitHub holds them in action_required, the approve API refuses them, and the March 2026 skip-approval setting covers the coding agent only (community #195881 asks for exactly this, unanswered). GitHub staff's recommended pattern for the gap IS a status-check gate like our polling job (#185265). Poll window raised to 15 min; probe removed. Escape hatch if the calculus changes (e.g. outside contributors post-Homebrew): a webhook-based GitHub App — pull_request_review webhooks fire regardless of actor; only Actions runs are trust-gated — posting a check run on the head SHA.

Pre-write on-disk check landed: write() inspects the file's bytes and refuses to overwrite content the storage has never seen, so a missed watcher event can no longer cost an external edit. Closes the EDIT case from this bead's description; the DELETION case (a save recreates a file deleted while the watcher missed it) survives and is tracked as pw-px7. Required beyond the bead's DESIGN, because that design did not account for the store handoff being asynchronous: an adoption gate (unacknowledgedAdoptions + acknowledgeExternalChange, renamed from cancelPendingSave) without which the protection lasted exactly one save and the quit flush clobbered the edit; and removal of the .unreadable guards from saveNow/scheduleSave, without which a suspension entered from the write path could only be lifted by the watcher this check exists to distrust. 409 Core tests, mutation-verified on the critical paths. Follow-ups: pw-px7, pw-ccx, pw-nmv, pw-5za.

Acknowledgement counter replaced by FileStorage.DocumentGeneration, minted only inside FileStorage.swift, handed out with every adopted external change, handed back on every save, compared at the write. Deletes unacknowledgedAdoptions, acknowledgeExternalChange(), its unmatched-call assertionFailure, and the test helper that reimplemented the store's half of the protocol. DELIBERATE DEVIATION from this bead's design note: it predicted loggedDetachedAdoption would disappear because 'a detached store never learns the new generation' — that would strand every later save on a generation nothing was told about, reintroducing the permanent latch pw-pkl fixed. The generation is the identity of the newest document HANDED TO SOMEONE, not a count of external changes, so it is bumped only on the delivering branch. load() returns (document, generation) so a rebuilt store rebases FORWARD; rewinding to .initial was tried and is wrong — it lets one value be minted twice and a stale holder then compares equal (ABA, proven by probe). Review found criticals in two successive fixes of mine, both from preferring a smaller edit over changing load()'s signature. 413 tests; 24 mutations run, every survivor now pinned. Follow-ups: pw-nmv (now unblocked), pw-ccx, pw-px7.
